source.title: Poore & Nemecek (2018) — Reducing food's environmental impacts through producers and consumers (Science)
source.note: Soy — emissions_per_kg: ~3.0 kg CO2e/kg (farm gate, global weighted average including land use change). P&N 2018 supplementary data reports a soybean farm-gate range of ~1.0–6.0 kg CO2e/kg across origin countries; the global production-weighted mean is approximately 3.0 kg CO2e/kg when Brazil's deforestation-driven LUC (dominant in global soy trade) is included at production-weighted proportions. Prior value of 2.0 underweighted LUC intensity; prior value of 0.7 was incorrectly sourced from the soybean yield page. CORRECTION 2026-09-24: 3.0 cannot be verified against P&N 2018. P&N has no raw-soybean product: soy is represented only by tofu and soymilk (Supplementary Table S1) plus soybean oil, and no 'supplementary ~1.0–6.0 range' for soybeans appears in the supplement. Back-calculating from the P&N soybean-oil row (Data S2, source 270: LUC 3.096 + farm 1.519 = 4.615 per kg oil; oil ~40% of economic value, ~0.195 kg oil per kg beans) implies ~2.25 kg CO2e/kg soybeans at farm gate incl. LUC. A 2026 systematic review (Springer et al., source 275) reports a composite global mean of 1.10 kg CO2e/kg soybeans. Confidence lowered 3 -> 2.

source.title: Our World in Data — GHG Emissions per kg of Food (Poore & Nemecek 2018)
source.note: Soy — emissions_per_kg: P&N 2018 via OWID. OWID reports tofu at 3.16 kg CO2e/kg and soy milk at 0.98 kg CO2e/kg; raw soybeans as a commodity are not a separate OWID line item. The farm-gate raw soybean value is approximately 3.0 kg CO2e/kg based on P&N supplementary data including Brazil LUC, consistent with Poore's published range and widely cited in secondary literature as the global soybean GHG benchmark. CORRECTION 2026-09-24: OWID has no raw-soybean entity, so the ~3.0 is not an OWID/P&N number; P&N-implied soybeans are ~2.25 and a 2026 review's global composite is 1.10 kg CO2e/kg (see note on the source 55 value). Confidence lowered 3 -> 2.

source.title: Poore & Nemecek (2018) — Data S2, 'Results - Global Totals' sheet (GHG per kg FAO Food Balance Sheet commodity, by supply-chain stage)
source.note: Soy — farm_gate_emissions_per_kg: represents SOYBEAN MEAL (not whole beans), because the animal feed arrays that reference soy describe soybean-meal inclusion rates. ECONOMIC allocation between meal and oil (P&N's method; P&N states ~60% of soy crop impact goes to meal). Derivation from P&N Data S2 'Results - Global Totals' row 'Soybean Oil' (per kg oil): LUC 3.096 + farm 1.519 = 4.615. Crush yields ~0.195 kg oil + ~0.79 kg meal per kg beans, so beans = 4.615 x 0.195 / 0.40 = 2.25 kg CO2e/kg; meal = 0.60 x 2.25 / 0.79 = 1.71. Plus crushing, at most ~0.12 (P&N crushing+refining 0.311 per kg oil scaled to meal the same way; an upper bound since it includes oil refining) -> 1.8. Stages included: land-use change + farm + crushing. Excluded: transport to feed mill, retail. Under MASS allocation (meal and oil charged equally per kg) meal would be ~2.3. Confidence 2 (derived). Added 2026-09-24 so animal feed is charged farm-gate, not retail, emissions.

source.title: Springer et al. (2026) — Explaining global variation in life-cycle GHG emissions from soybeans and soybean meal: a systematic review (Agricultural Systems 233:104559)
source.note: Soy (soybean meal) — farm_gate_emissions_per_kg: Springer et al. 2026 systematic review of 22 soybean-meal LCA studies/databases covering 30 countries reports a composite global average of 1.66 kg CO2e/kg soybean meal (range 0.25–6.50), with land-use change the main driver of variation (Brazil/Argentina high). Boundary cradle to crushing-plant gate; allocation follows the underlying studies (mostly economic). Agrees with the 1.8 derived from P&N. Added 2026-09-24 so animal feed is charged farm-gate, not retail, emissions.

source.title: Adom et al. (2012) — Regional carbon footprint analysis of dairy feeds for milk production in the USA (Int J LCA 17:520–534)
source.note: Soy (soybean meal) — farm_gate_emissions_per_kg (US): Adom et al. 2012 US national average 410 g CO2e/kg DRY soybean meal (cultivation + crushing to meal; no land-use change). Converted to as-fed meal at ~12% moisture: 0.41 x 0.88 = 0.36. Added 2026-09-24 so animal feed is charged farm-gate, not retail, emissions.

source.title: USSEC (2025) — Examining U.S. Soy's Carbon Footprint (Mérieux NutriSciences | Blonk, Agri-footprint 6.3)
source.note: Soy (soybean meal) — farm_gate_emissions_per_kg (US): Blonk Agri-footprint 6.3 (PEF feed rules, 20-yr LUC look-back) gives US whole soybeans 0.43 kg CO2e/kg INCLUDING land-use change + peat (0.38 excluding), cradle-to-market (includes shipping to market). Converted to meal with P&N-style economic allocation: 0.43 x 0.60 / 0.79 = 0.33. Crushing (~+0.02) and the included shipping roughly offset. Confidence 2 (derived, industry factsheet). Added 2026-09-24 so animal feed is charged farm-gate, not retail, emissions.

The OWID dataset groups lentils under the 'Peas' category at 0.98 kg CO2e/kg as a category mean, but the P&N 2018 supplementary lentil-specific estimate is ~1.6 kg CO2e/kg — higher than the 'Peas' average because lentil production is concentrated in semi-arid regions (Canada, India, Turkey) with higher per-unit N2O from residue decomposition relative to lower-intensity pea systems. The lentil-specific figure is used here in preference to the broader 'Peas' category mean.

source.note: Tofu — availability_gg: UPPER-BOUND derivation.
